question: An 18-year-old boy who went to the emergency room due to pain and functional impotence in the right knee. After the biopsy study, the diagnosis of osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the distal femur is established. Given the type of tumor and the location, what treatment protocol is usually performed in most cases?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the distal femur -> High-grade malignant bone tumor -> Requires aggressive treatment -> 95% CHAIN: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy -> Reduces tumor size before surgery -> Improves surgical outcomes -> 90% CHAIN: Surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy -> Removes the remaining tumor -> Helps prevent recurrence -> 85% CHAIN: Adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery -> Destroys any remaining cancer cells -> Reduces the risk of metastasis -> 80% CHAIN: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy -> Surgery -> Adjuvant chemotherapy -> Standard treatment protocol for osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the distal femur -> 95%
